answer: Pay only for verified work, never for account count. Each accepted result enters one audit thread keyed to a unique input; the ledger treats every account as a billing vertex, and a checker pays p per result, adding a violet rejection marker for duplicate submissions. If one operator splits one quantity of work across n accounts, total pay over the period stays p times verified results, so extra identities add aggregate reward only by producing more real, checkable output. Assumption: an independent checker verifies output; colluding reviewers remain the weakness.
